model.name: Provenance
model.purpose: Governed mixin for the recorded history of origin, derivation, influence, responsibility, custody, generation, usage, invalidation and attestation of a subject, so an agent can create, inspect, validate and operate provenance independently of storage format.
model.scope_statement: This mixin captures what happened to a subject, who or what was responsible, which prior entities influenced it, when and where those events occurred, how the resulting record is bound and attested, and how that record is discovered, validated, redacted, retained or invalidated. It is mixed into other world-model subjects rather than replacing them. Serialization, transport and query interfaces are projections of these semantics, not the model.
in_scope: Identity of a provenance record and binding of that record to a subject, including constrained views, specializations and alternates of the same thing.
Core types Entity, Activity and Agent and the relations generation, usage, communication, start, end, invalidation, derivation, attribution, association, delegation and influence.
Lineage as sources and process steps, including ingredients, resolved dependencies and build or transformation definitions.
Responsibility, role, plan, delegation, claim-generator identity and signer identity as they affect the provenance record.
Custody and ownership history insofar as they are significant for authenticity, integrity and interpretation.
Event times, observation or ingestion times, ordering constraints, and locations of entities, activities, agents or instantaneous events.
Cryptographic or other content bindings, signed attestations, timestamps, revocation status, completeness and accuracy claims, and redaction of assertions.
Named bundles or manifests that support provenance of provenance, plus discovery, query, pingback, access, privacy and retention of the provenance record itself.
out_of_scope: Authoritative identity, legal personhood, employment or contact data of agents as a Party or Identity model; this mixin only records the agent as a responsibility-bearing participant.
The subject's own lifecycle, versioning policy or business state machine beyond the provenance events that generated, used or invalidated a characterized entity.
Rights, licences, copyright status and permissions as a Rights model; PREMIS Rights and Dublin Core rights terms are referenced, not owned.
Access-control policy, authentication and authorization as an Access or Security model, except the access metadata of the provenance record.
Quality scores, fitness-for-use metrics and data-quality reports as a Quality model; lineage may be used to assess quality but does not store quality results.
Generic calendar events, incidents or workflow instances that are not generation, usage, invalidation, start, end or other provenance activities.
Geospatial features, coordinate reference systems and place gazetteers as a Location model; only the location of a provenance event or characterized entity is in scope.
Software bill of materials composition (what is inside an artifact) as a Composition or SBOM model; only how the artifact was produced is in scope.
Value judgements that a record is authentic, trustworthy, good or bad; C2PA and PROV supply evidence and constraints, not a verdict.
Courtroom chain-of-custody procedure, seizure documentation and expert-witness testimony as a Forensic Evidence model.
Training-data governance, model cards and AI safety evaluations as an ML-governance model; AI disclosure is an alignment, not an owned subtree.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Agent, Party or Actor identity model
boundary_notes.distinction: PROV-DM and PREMIS treat an agent as something that bears responsibility for an activity, entity or other agent, typed as person, organization or software. Full identity, contact, legal status and organizational structure belong in a sibling Party model; this mixin only records the identifier, type, version, role and responsibility links needed to interpret provenance.

Dublin Core and PREMIS treat rights, licences and rightsHolders as statements that may be part of a resource's history, but they are not the provenance graph. This mixin may point at a rights statement that constrained use or derivation; it does not encode copyright, licence terms or permission grants.

ISO 19115 historically nested lineage under data quality, then ISO 19115-1 detached LI_Lineage from DQ_DataQuality. Provenance supports quality assessment but does not store accuracy, completeness or conformance measures of the subject.

PROV permits prov:location on entities, activities, agents and instantaneous events; CIDOC models E9 Move and E53 Place; EPCIS records where an event happened. Geometry, CRS and gazetteer identity belong in a Location model. This mixin only records the location that situates a provenance event or characterized entity.

A provenance activity is something that occurs over a period and acts upon entities. PREMIS Event, EPCIS event types, CIDOC E7 Activity and C2PA actions are alignments of that idea. A generic event bus, incident, meeting or calendar occurrence is out of scope unless it generated, used, invalidated or transferred a subject.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Digital Object, Artifact or Dataset model
boundary_notes.distinction: The subject of provenance is an entity in another model. This mixin binds to that subject and records how a characterized snapshot came to be; it does not own content bytes, schema, media type or dataset variables.

SLSA provenance and in-toto statements describe where, when and how an artifact was produced and may list resolvedDependencies. SPDX or CycloneDX SBOMs describe what is inside the artifact. Composition of contents is a sibling; production history is this mixin.

PROV-AQ and OAIS Access Rights Information govern how provenance records are located and who may read them. Policy engines, ACLs and authentication protocols belong in an Access model. This mixin records access metadata, sensitivity and exceptions for the provenance record.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Forensic evidence and legal chain-of-custody model
boundary_notes.distinction: CIDOC separates legal ownership (E8 Acquisition) from physical custody (E10 Transfer of Custody). Dublin Core provenance is a statement of ownership and custody changes significant for authenticity. This mixin records those transfers as provenance facts. Courtroom exhibits, seizure logs and expert-witness procedure remain a sibling Forensic Evidence model and are a known omission where no primary forensic standard was adopted here.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Normative domain-agnostic data model for provenance as entities, activities and agents, with generation, usage, derivation, attribution, association, delegation, bundles, specialization, alternate and collections.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: OWL2 encoding of PROV-DM, including starting-point, expanded and qualified terms, agent subtypes, plans, roles, locations and instantaneous events.

sources.title: Constraints of the PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Defines valid provenance via uniqueness, event-ordering, typing and impossibility constraints, plus normalization and equivalence of instances and bundles.

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Preservation metadata model of Objects, Events, Agents and Rights; digital provenance as documented actions that modify objects; identifiers, eventDateTime, outcomes and linking roles.

sources.title: Content Credentials : C2PA Technical Specification
sources.organization: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA)
sources.relevance: Cryptographically bound content provenance: assertions, claims, claim signatures, manifests, hard and soft bindings, redaction, trust lists, time-stamps, ingredients, actions and AI disclosure.

sources.title: SLSA Build Provenance
sources.relevance: Verifiable software provenance describing where, when and how artifacts were produced: buildDefinition, runDetails, builder trust boundary, resolvedDependencies, timestamps and verification.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms: Provenance
sources.version_or_date: DCMI Metadata Terms, current release 2020-01-20 aligned to ISO 15836-2:2019
sources.relevance: Defines dcterms:provenance as a statement of ownership and custody changes significant for authenticity, integrity and interpretation, ranging to ProvenanceStatement.

sources.title: EPCIS and Core Business Vocabulary
sources.version_or_date: EPCIS / CBV 2.0, ratified June 2022; also ISO/IEC 19987
sources.relevance: Event-based traceability capturing what, when, where, why and how of products and assets, including chain of custody and transformation across supply chains.

sources.title: Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model
sources.organization: CIDOC CRM Special Interest Group / ICOM
sources.relevance: Separates legal ownership (E8 Acquisition) from physical custody (E10 Transfer of Custody) and models modification, movement and actor participation in cultural-heritage provenance.

sources.title: ISO 14721:2025 Space Data System Practices — Reference model for an open archival information system (OAIS)
sources.version_or_date: ISO 14721:2025 (third edition), based on CCSDS 650.0-M-3 December 2024
sources.relevance: OAIS Preservation Description Information includes Provenance Information as origin, changes and custody of Content Information, together with Reference, Context, Fixity and Access Rights Information.

sources.title: in-toto Attestation Framework
sources.relevance: Authenticated metadata about software artifacts: Envelope, Statement and Predicate layers used by SLSA provenance and other supply-chain attestations.

sources.title: ISO 19115-1:2014 Geographic information — Metadata — Part 1: Fundamentals
sources.relevance: Defines lineage as provenance, sources and production processes (LI_Lineage, LI_ProcessStep, LI_Source) and distinguishes that sense of provenance from ISO 5127's organisational meaning.

sources.title: PROV-AQ: Provenance Access and Query
sources.relevance: Mechanisms to locate, retrieve and query provenance records via HTTP Link relations, HTML and RDF, query services and pingback, plus security considerations for trust in records.

sources.title: Dublin Core to PROV Mapping
sources.relevance: Partial mapping of Dublin Core agency, date and derivation terms to PROV, and the special status of dct:provenance as a link to a ProvenanceStatement rather than a graph edge.

bundles.name: Subject and record identity
bundles.description: Identity of a provenance record and the subject it describes, including constrained views, specializations and alternates of the same underlying thing.
bundles.rationale: PROV, PROV-AQ and C2PA all require a distinct identifier for the record and a target identifier for the entity described; without that binding, provenance cannot be interpreted or verified.

layers.name: Provenance record identity
layers.description: How a provenance record, bundle, manifest or statement is identified, typed and distinguished from the subject it describes.

findings.name: Provenance record identifier
findings.description: A provenance record is itself an entity: a named set of assertions (PROV Bundle, C2PA Manifest, in-toto Statement, PREMIS event set or EPCIS event) that must have a master-system identifier or IRI, a type, and a generation identity independent of the subject.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this provenance record, and which system assigned it?
What kind of provenance record is this (bundle, manifest, attestation statement, preservation event set, traceability event)?
When was this record generated, by which generator, and at what observation or ingestion time was it received here?
What namespace, IRI or URN scheme governs identifiers inside this record, and is a Dimension UUID or ULID used only as a fallback?

data_elements.name: Record identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the provenance record in the master system that minted it.

data_elements.name: Governed global IRI
data_elements.description: Globally unique IRI, URN or qualified name for the record when one exists.

data_elements.name: Record kind
data_elements.description: Coded type of the record such as prov:Bundle, C2PA Manifest, in-toto Statement or PREMIS event.

data_elements.name: Record generation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant when the record itself was generated.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant when this Dimension observed or ingested the record, distinct from event time.

artifacts.name: Provenance record artifact
artifacts.description: Serializable named set of provenance assertions treated as an entity so that provenance of provenance can be expressed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Prefer the minting system's identifier; else a governed IRI such as a C2PA URN or prov qualified name; else a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. A date is not an identifier.

layers.name: Subject binding
layers.description: How a provenance record points at the subject entity, including constrained resources, specializations and alternates.

findings.name: Subject and target binding
findings.description: A provenance record is about one or more target entities. PROV-AQ distinguishes resource URI, target-URI and provenance-URI. C2PA binds a manifest to asset content via hard or soft bindings. SLSA identifies subjects by cryptographic digest.

questions.text: Which subject entity does this record describe, and is that identifier the resource URI, a versioned target-URI, or a digest?
Does the record describe the whole asset, a constrained view, a byte range, a live-video segment, or a collection member?
If several target identifiers are present, which identifiers must a consumer isolate before interpreting assertions?

data_elements.name: Subject identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the entity whose provenance is recorded.

data_elements.name: Subject digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest uniquely identifying the subject bytes or package when a content binding is used.

data_elements.name: Target URI
data_elements.description: URI used inside the provenance record to denote the described constrained resource.

data_elements.name: Binding kind
data_elements.description: Whether the record is bound by identifier, hard hash, soft fingerprint or watermark.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The binding is a set of identifiers, digests and coded relations held on the record; it is not a separate stored document unless a hard-binding assertion is serialised inside a C2PA or SLSA artifact already covered elsewhere.

findings.name: Specialization and alternate entities
findings.description: Different entities may fix different aspects of the same thing. specializationOf links a more specific entity to a more general one; alternateOf links entities presenting aspects of the same thing, possibly at different times or in different formats.

questions.text: Is this entity a specialization of a more general resource, and which fixed aspects distinguish it?
Which alternate entities present other aspects of the same thing, such as another format or revision snapshot?
Which attributes are fixed for the lifetime of this entity, and would a change require a new entity identifier?

data_elements.name: Specialization of
data_elements.description: Reference to a more general entity of which this entity presents additional fixed aspects.

data_elements.name: Alternate of
data_elements.description: Reference to another entity presenting aspects of the same thing.

data_elements.name: Fixed aspects
data_elements.description: Attribute set that holds for the entire lifetime of the entity.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Specialization and alternate are graph relations with optional attribute maps; they are inline unless a Dimension chooses to serialise an entity characterization sheet as a separate artifact.

bundles.name: Core provenance graph
bundles.description: The core types Entity, Activity and Agent and the relations that connect use, production, start, end and invalidation.
bundles.rationale: PROV-DM defines these as the essence of provenance; PREMIS, C2PA, SLSA and EPCIS specialise the same triangle of thing, process and responsible party.

layers.name: Entity, activity and agent
layers.description: Characterization of the three core types and their allowed overlap.

findings.name: Entity
findings.description: An entity is a physical, digital, conceptual or other thing with some fixed aspects; it may be real or imaginary, and its lifetime is delimited by generation and invalidation.

questions.text: What identifier and types describe this entity, and is it also typed as an agent, collection, plan or bundle?
When was this entity generated and, if applicable, invalidated, and by which activities?
Is a literal value a direct representation of this entity, and what location if any situates it?

data_elements.name: Entity identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the characterized entity.

data_elements.name: Entity types
data_elements.description: PROV and domain types such as Collection, Bundle, Plan or a domain class.

data_elements.name: Entity label
data_elements.description: Human-readable label.

data_elements.name: Entity value
data_elements.description: Literal direct representation of the entity when applicable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: An entity characterization is inline graph data unless the entity is itself a stored digital object owned by a sibling Artifact model.

findings.name: Activity
findings.description: An activity occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities, including consuming, processing, transforming, modifying, relocating, using or generating them.

questions.text: What identifier, type and plan describe this activity?
When did this activity start and end, and which entities started or ended it?
Does this activity align to a PREMIS eventType, C2PA action, EPCIS event type, ISO process step or SLSA buildType?

data_elements.name: Activity identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the activity.

data_elements.name: Activity type
data_elements.description: Typed classification of the activity.

data_elements.name: Start time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant the activity started.

data_elements.name: End time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant the activity ended.

data_elements.name: Plan
data_elements.description: Entity representing the intended steps, workflow, style sheet, policy or build type.

artifacts.name: Activity execution by-product
artifacts.description: Logs or resolved configuration generated during an activity that are not the primary output but are useful for debugging or incident response.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by the activity's master identifier plus a by-product digest or URI; do not use timestamps as identifiers.

findings.name: Agent
findings.description: An agent bears some form of responsibility for an activity, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity, and may be a person, organization or software agent.

questions.text: What identifier and agent type (person, organization, software) identify this responsibility-bearer?
Is the agent's own provenance in scope, and which entity identifier represents the agent as a thing with history?
Does this identifier also denote an activity, and if so does that violate disjointness constraints?

data_elements.name: Agent identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the agent.

data_elements.name: Agent type
data_elements.description: Person, organization, software agent or domain extension.

data_elements.name: Agent name
data_elements.description: Display name of the agent.

data_elements.name: Agent version
data_elements.description: Version of a software agent when relevant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Agent identity used in provenance is a compact reference; detailed party records live in a sibling Party model.

layers.name: Generation, usage and lifetime events
layers.description: Relations that connect activities to entities at the instants of production, use, start, end and invalidation.

findings.name: Generation, usage and communication
findings.description: Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. Usage is the beginning of utilizing an entity. Communication is exchange of some unspecified entity between two activities.

questions.text: Which activity generated this entity, at what time, and in what role?
Which entities did this activity use, at what times, and did usage consume them?
Was this activity informed by another activity, implying an unspecified exchanged entity?
Is there at most one generation of this entity in this instance, as required for valid PROV?

data_elements.name: Generation identifier
data_elements.description: Optional identifier of a generation event.

data_elements.name: Usage identifier
data_elements.description: Optional identifier of a usage event.

data_elements.name: Generation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of generation.

data_elements.name: Usage time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant usage began.

data_elements.name: Role
data_elements.description: Function of an entity or agent with respect to an activity in a usage, generation or association.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Generation, usage and communication are qualified relations; they are inline graph data unless bundled into a named provenance artifact.

findings.name: Start, end and invalidation
findings.description: Activities are delimited by start and end events; entities cease to be available after invalidation. These instantaneous events carry optional times and triggering entities or activities.

questions.text: Which entity or activity started this activity, and at what time?
Which entity or activity ended this activity, and at what time?
Which activity invalidated this entity, at what time, and is the entity no longer available for use?

data_elements.name: Invalidation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant after which the entity no longer exists for use.

data_elements.name: Invalidating activity
data_elements.description: Activity that invalidated the entity.

data_elements.name: Activity start event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of the start event when distinct from activity startedAtTime.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Start, end and invalidation are instantaneous events represented as qualified relations, not independent documents.

bundles.name: Derivation and lineage
bundles.description: How entities are transformed from other entities, including derivation subtypes, process steps, sources, ingredients and build inputs.
bundles.rationale: PROV derivation, ISO 19115 lineage, C2PA ingredients and actions, SLSA resolvedDependencies and EPCIS TransformationEvent all record how a thing came from prior things.

layers.name: Derivation and subtypes
layers.description: Transformation, update or construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity, including revision, quotation and primary source.

findings.name: Derivation, revision, quotation and primary source
findings.description: A derivation connects a generated entity to a used entity with some influence. Revision, quotation and primary source are typed derivations. Usage plus generation is necessary but not sufficient.

questions.text: From which entity or entities was this entity derived, and what derivation type applies?
Which activity, generation and usage instantiate this derivation when the relation is expanded?
Is a primary source asserted, meaning an agent with direct experience produced the used entity?
Is this a revision of substantial content, a quotation, a format alternate, or only a weaker Dublin Core version or reference relation?

data_elements.name: Derivation identifier
data_elements.description: Optional identifier of the derivation relation.

data_elements.name: Used entity
data_elements.description: Entity that influenced the generated entity.

data_elements.name: Generated entity
data_elements.description: Entity produced by the derivation.

data_elements.name: Derivation type
data_elements.description: Revision, quotation, primary source or generic derivation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Derivation is a typed graph edge, optionally qualified with activity, generation and usage; it is inline unless exported as part of a provenance record artifact.

layers.name: Process steps, sources and ingredients
layers.description: Lineage as a sequence of process steps using sources, plus software and media ingredients.

findings.name: Process steps and sources
findings.description: ISO 19115 LI_Lineage aggregates a statement, LI_Source records and LI_ProcessStep records with description, rationale, dateTime and processor. At least one of statement, source or processStep must be present at dataset scope.

questions.text: What general explanation of lineage is known when detailed sources or steps are absent?
What process steps were applied, when, by which processors, with what rationale and software or algorithm?
Which source resources were used, with what citations, extents and processed levels?

data_elements.name: Lineage statement
data_elements.description: General explanation of the producer's knowledge of lineage.

data_elements.name: Process step description
data_elements.description: Description of an event or transformation in the life of the resource.

data_elements.name: Process step date-time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of the process step.

data_elements.name: Source citation
data_elements.description: Citation of a source resource.

artifacts.name: Lineage or process-step report
artifacts.description: Documented lineage statement, process-step reports and source citations for a dataset or other resource.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by the resource's master identifier plus a lineage record identifier; prefer ISO metadata file identifiers when present.

findings.name: Ingredients, dependencies and build definition
findings.description: C2PA ingredients and actions, SLSA buildDefinition with externalParameters, internalParameters and resolvedDependencies, and in-toto subjects describe inputs used to produce an output.

questions.text: Which ingredient assets or resolved dependencies were used, and do they carry their own provenance manifests?
What buildType or action sequence produced the output, and which parameters were external versus platform-internal?
Are resolved dependencies complete, best-effort, or known incomplete, and which transitive fetches are missing?

data_elements.name: Build type
data_elements.description: URI identifying the template for how to perform the build and interpret parameters.

data_elements.name: External parameters
data_elements.description: Untrusted parameters under external control that must be recorded and verified downstream.

data_elements.name: Resolved dependencies
data_elements.description: Artifacts needed at build or composition time, with URI and digest.

data_elements.name: Ingredient reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an ingredient asset and optional nested manifest.

artifacts.name: Build provenance predicate
artifacts.description: SLSA or in-toto provenance predicate describing how an artifact set was produced.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify subjects by cryptographic digest; identify the builder by builder.id URI; identify the invocation by builder-defined invocationId.

bundles.name: Responsibility and custody
bundles.description: Who or what was responsible, under what plan and role, who held custody or title, and who signed or generated the claim.
bundles.rationale: Trust assessments depend on responsibility. PROV attribution, association and delegation, PREMIS agent roles, CIDOC acquisition versus custody, DCMI provenance, and C2PA signer identity cover that surface.

layers.name: Attribution, association and delegation
layers.description: Ascribing entities to agents, assigning responsibility for activities, and delegating authority while retaining residual responsibility.

findings.name: Attribution, association and delegation
findings.description: Attribution ascribes an entity to an agent. Association assigns responsibility for an activity and may cite a plan and role. Delegation assigns authority to a delegate while the responsible agent retains some responsibility.

questions.text: To which agents is this entity attributed, and in which roles such as creator, contributor or publisher?
Which agents were associated with this activity, with what roles and plans?
On whose behalf did this agent act, and for which activity does residual responsibility remain?

data_elements.name: Attributed agent
data_elements.description: Agent to which the entity is ascribed.

data_elements.name: Associated agent
data_elements.description: Agent assigned responsibility for an activity.

data_elements.name: Responsible agent in delegation
data_elements.description: Agent that retains responsibility while a delegate acts.

data_elements.name: Had role
data_elements.description: Role played in an association, usage or generation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Responsibility relations are qualified graph edges. Agent details beyond identifier, type, version and role belong in a Party sibling.

layers.name: Custody and ownership history
layers.description: Changes in physical custody and legal title that are significant for authenticity, integrity and interpretation.

findings.name: Custody and ownership chain
findings.description: Dublin Core provenance is a statement of ownership and custody changes. CIDOC models E8 Acquisition (legal title) separately from E10 Transfer of Custody (physical custody), including beginning, end, unknown-source, loss and involuntary transfer. EPCIS records chain-of-custody events. OAIS Provenance Information includes who has had custody since origin.

questions.text: Who currently has physical custody or legal responsibility for custody of the subject?
Who currently holds legal title, and is title distinct from custody?
What transfers of custody or title occurred, from whom to whom, when, where, and were they voluntary, unknown-source, loss or theft?
Which custody or ownership changes are significant for authenticity, integrity or interpretation, and which successive custodians altered the resource?

data_elements.name: Custodian
data_elements.description: Actor currently holding physical custody or legal custody responsibility.

data_elements.name: Title holder
data_elements.description: Actor holding legal ownership.

data_elements.name: Transfer kind
data_elements.description: Acquisition, custody transfer, beginning, end, unknown source, loss, theft or involuntary transfer.

data_elements.name: Narrative provenance statement
data_elements.description: Statement of ownership and custody changes significant for authenticity, integrity and interpretation.

artifacts.name: Custody and title register
artifacts.description: Chronological register of custody and title transfers, optionally accompanied by a narrative ProvenanceStatement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each transfer event uses the master event identifier from the custody system or EPCIS event ID; the register as a whole uses the subject's identifier plus a register version.

layers.name: Claim generator and signer
layers.description: The hardware or software that generated the claim and the credential holder that signed it, distinct from content creators.

findings.name: Claim generator, signer and builder
findings.description: C2PA distinguishes claim generator, signer and actor. SLSA builder.id is the transitive closure of the trusted build platform. Signer identity is the basis of the C2PA trust model and must be paired with accepted builder identities for SLSA.

questions.text: Which hardware or software generated the claim, on which operating system, and against which specification version?
Who is the credential holder that signed the claim, and which certificate, EKU and trust list apply?
What builder.id represents the trusted platform, and which fields were tenant-generated rather than control-plane-generated?

data_elements.name: Claim generator
data_elements.description: Non-human actor that generated the claim and signature.

data_elements.name: Signer
data_elements.description: Credential holder of the private key used to sign.

data_elements.name: Builder identity
data_elements.description: URI indicating the transitive closure of the trusted build platform.

data_elements.name: Specification version
data_elements.description: Version of C2PA, SLSA or other spec used to generate the record.

artifacts.name: Signing credential
artifacts.description: X.509 certificate or equivalent credential used to sign a claim, plus optional time-stamp token.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify certificates by issuer and serial number or SKI; identify builders by builder.id URI. Do not treat signature time as an identifier.

bundles.name: Time and place
bundles.description: Event time versus observation time, clocks, ordering constraints, and locations of provenance events.
bundles.rationale: PROV is based on instantaneous events and minimizes global-clock assumptions; SLSA, PREMIS, C2PA and EPCIS still require explicit timestamps and often locations.

layers.name: Times and ordering
layers.description: When events happened, how they are ordered, and how clocks are treated.

findings.name: Event times, observation times and ordering
findings.description: PROV uses events rather than a single global timeline. Valid instances satisfy precedes and strictly-precedes constraints such as generation before usage and start before end. PREMIS requires eventDateTime. C2PA uses RFC 3339. Observation or ingestion time of a record is distinct from event time.

questions.text: What is the event time of this generation, usage, invalidation, start, end or other provenance event, with seconds and explicit offset or Z?
When was this fact observed or ingested, and is that distinct from the event time?
Do the events in this instance satisfy generation-before-usage, start-before-end and related ordering constraints, or is the instance invalid?
Which clock produced this timestamp, and is cross-system alignment only partial?

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the provenance event.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the fact was observed.

data_elements.name: PREMIS eventDateTime
data_elements.description: Mandatory date-time of a preservation event when using PREMIS alignment.

data_elements.name: Ordering validity
data_elements.description: Result of checking event-ordering constraints.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Times and ordering results are attributes of events and constraint checks, stored inline on the record.

layers.name: Provenance location
layers.description: Where an entity, activity, agent or instantaneous event was situated.

findings.name: Location of provenance events
findings.description: PROV allows prov:location on entities, activities, agents and instantaneous events. EPCIS treats where as a core event dimension. Detailed geometry belongs in a Location sibling.

questions.text: Where did this activity or event occur, in what location identifier or description?
At which location is this characterized entity situated during its lifetime?
Is the location only a reference to a Place model, or is an inline label sufficient?

data_elements.name: At location
data_elements.description: Reference to a location of an entity, activity, agent or event.

data_elements.name: Location label
data_elements.description: Inline human-readable location when a Place identifier is unavailable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Location in this mixin is a reference or short label; geometries and gazetteers live in a Location sibling.

bundles.name: Integrity, attestation and evidence
bundles.description: How a record is bound to content, signed, timestamped, trusted, completed, redacted or found invalid.
bundles.rationale: C2PA, SLSA, in-toto and OAIS Fixity Information make provenance usable as evidence. Without binding and attestation, a history can be forged or detached.

layers.name: Content binding and fixity
layers.description: Hard hashes, soft fingerprints and watermarks that associate a record with content, plus OAIS fixity.

findings.name: Hard binding, soft binding and fixity
findings.description: C2PA hard bindings are cryptographic hashes of whole or partial assets; soft bindings are fingerprints or watermarks used to recover detached manifests. OAIS Fixity Information documents integrity. SLSA identifies subjects by digest.

questions.text: What hash algorithm and hash values bind this record to which byte ranges or boxes of the asset?
Is a fingerprint or watermark present that can recover a detached manifest from a repository?
Has fixity been verified against the recorded hashes, and what is the current integrity state?

data_elements.name: Hash algorithm
data_elements.description: Algorithm used for a hard binding.

data_elements.name: Hash value
data_elements.description: Digest value of bound content.

data_elements.name: Soft binding
data_elements.description: Fingerprint or watermark identifier.

data_elements.name: Fixity status
data_elements.description: Result of comparing current content to recorded hashes.

artifacts.name: Content binding assertion
artifacts.description: Hard-binding or soft-binding structure associating a provenance record with asset bytes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by the containing manifest identifier plus assertion label; hashes identify content, not the binding record.

layers.name: Signed attestation and trust
layers.description: Signatures, time-stamps, trust lists, SLSA levels and validation states.

findings.name: Signed attestation and trust state
findings.description: A C2PA Manifest is well-formed, valid or trusted according to signature, time-stamp, revocation and trust-list checks. SLSA Build levels constrain authenticity, accuracy and completeness of provenance. in-toto envelopes authenticate statements. Trust in a provenance record is distinct from trust in the original resource.

questions.text: Does the claim signature verify, was it made while the credential was valid, and is revocation information current?
Which trust list and TSA trust list were used, and is the signer an accepted pair with the builder or claim generator?
What SLSA Build level is claimed or verified, and does provenance authenticity meet the corresponding bar?
Is the manifest well-formed, valid, trusted, or only partially interpretable due to unknown constructs?

data_elements.name: Signature status
data_elements.description: Outcome of signature verification.

data_elements.name: Trust list
data_elements.description: Identifier of the trust list used for validation.

data_elements.name: SLSA Build level
data_elements.description: Claimed or verified SLSA Build level.

data_elements.name: Manifest state
data_elements.description: Well-formed, valid, trusted, or invalid.

artifacts.name: Signed attestation
artifacts.description: Envelope plus statement plus predicate that can be verified independently of the subject store.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by statement subject digest plus predicateType and signer credential; invocationId may further distinguish build runs.

layers.name: Completeness, redaction and constraint validity
layers.description: Whether the record is complete, accurate, redacted, or invalid under provenance constraints.

findings.name: Completeness, redaction and constraint validity
findings.description: SLSA distinguishes completeness, authenticity and accuracy. C2PA allows redaction of assertions with a declaration. PROV-CONSTRAINTS defines valid instances via uniqueness, ordering, typing and impossibility constraints. Absence of information is not the same as a negative fact.

questions.text: Is this record asserted complete, best-effort, or known incomplete, and which expected fields are absent?
Which assertions were redacted, by whom, and is the redaction declared so that hashes still verify?
Does this instance satisfy uniqueness, typing, impossibility and event-ordering constraints after normalization?
Has any consumer inferred that valid provenance means the content is authentic or good, contrary to C2PA non-goals?

data_elements.name: Completeness claim
data_elements.description: Complete, best-effort or incomplete.

data_elements.name: Redacted assertions
data_elements.description: Identifiers of assertions removed after signing, with declaration.

data_elements.name: PROV validity status
data_elements.description: Valid, invalid or not checked against PROV-CONSTRAINTS.

artifacts.name: Validation report
artifacts.description: Machine-readable result of signature, constraint and completeness checks, including advisory codes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by the record identifier plus validator identity and validation time; validation time is not the record identifier.

bundles.name: Access, retention and interoperability
bundles.description: How provenance records are discovered, queried, pinged back, accessed, retained, deleted and aligned across standards.
bundles.rationale: PROV-AQ, OAIS Access Rights, C2PA privacy goals and the many partial mappings among PROV, Dublin Core, PREMIS, C2PA, SLSA, CIDOC, ISO 19115 and EPCIS define the operating surface for sharing provenance.

layers.name: Discovery, query and pingback
layers.description: Locating provenance-URIs, query services and downstream usage reports.

findings.name: Locating, querying and pingback
findings.description: PROV-AQ defines has_provenance, has_query_service and pingback link relations, plus HTTP and SPARQL query services. Multiple providers may offer contradictory records. Pingback discovers downstream usage the original publisher did not know.

questions.text: Where can this provenance record be retrieved, and which target-URI does that record use for the subject?
Which query service can return provenance for this target, and what URI template or SPARQL endpoint does it expose?
Is a pingback URI published, and which downstream provenance-URIs have been posted against it?
Do multiple providers offer provenance about the same target, and how should contradictions be handled?

data_elements.name: Provenance URI
data_elements.description: URI denoting a provenance record.

data_elements.name: Query service URI
data_elements.description: URI of a provenance query service.

data_elements.name: Pingback URI
data_elements.description: URI that accepts POST of additional provenance-URIs.

artifacts.name: Provenance query service description
artifacts.description: RDF or other description of direct HTTP and SPARQL provenance query mechanisms.

layers.name: Access, privacy, retention and alignment
layers.description: Who may see the record, how long it is kept, and how competing standards are aligned without false conformance.

findings.name: Access, privacy and retention of provenance records
findings.description: C2PA design goals include user control over whether provenance data is included. OAIS Access Rights Information is part of PDI. PROV-AQ notes that existence of a resource may be sensitive. ISO 14721:2025 allows ingest-first with optional PDI. Records themselves may be invalidated, redacted or deleted under policy.

questions.text: Who may read this provenance record or specific layers, findings or artifacts, and what is the default deny or allow rule?
Did the creator withhold or redact personal or sensitive provenance fields, and under which privacy basis?
How long must this record be retained, when may it be deleted or invalidated, and does archive policy require preserving provenance of deletions?
Would disclosing that a provenance record exists itself leak sensitive information, requiring a non-404 denial?

data_elements.name: Default access rule
data_elements.description: Default allow or deny for the provenance record.

data_elements.name: Withheld fields
data_elements.description: Fields omitted by creator control.

data_elements.name: Retain until
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant or policy code when retention ends.

data_elements.name: Legal hold
data_elements.description: Whether deletion is blocked by hold.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Access, privacy and retention are policy attributes of the record. The policies themselves may be documents in a Policy sibling; this mixin stores the effective constraints on the provenance record.

functions.name: Assert generation
functions.description: Record that an activity completed production of a new entity at an optional time and role.
preconditions: Entity and activity identifiers exist or are minted.
If time is present it is RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z.
effects: Adds a generation relation.
May infer entity type and activity type.
Unique-generation constraint becomes checkable.

functions.name: Assert usage
functions.description: Record that an activity began to utilize an entity at an optional time and role.
preconditions: Generation of the entity, if known, does not strictly follow this usage.
effects: Adds a usage relation.
Supports later derivation and communication inferences.

functions.name: Assert derivation
functions.description: Record that a generated entity was influenced by a used entity, optionally expanded with activity, generation and usage, and optionally typed as revision, quotation or primary source.
preconditions: Influence is determined by the asserter; usage plus generation alone is not sufficient.
effects: Adds a derivation edge.
May infer alternateOf for revisions.

functions.name: Attribute entity to agent
functions.description: Ascribe an entity to an agent, optionally with a qualified role such as creator or publisher.
preconditions: Agent identifier is known at least as a responsibility-bearer.
effects: Adds attribution.
Does not create a full Party record.

functions.name: Associate activity with agent
functions.description: Assign responsibility for an activity to an agent, optionally citing a plan and role.
effects: Adds association.
Plan entity may itself become a provenance subject.

functions.name: Record custody or title transfer
functions.description: Record beginning, end or transfer of physical custody or legal title, including unknown-source and involuntary cases.
preconditions: Custody and title are not conflated unless the adopting Dimension documents that collapse.
effects: Appends a transfer event.
Updates current custodian or title holder.
May add a narrative provenance statement.

functions.name: Issue signed attestation
functions.description: Generate a claim over assertions or a provenance predicate, bind it to subject digests, and sign with a credential.
preconditions: Claim generator is authorized to use the signer credential.
Hash algorithm is an accepted algorithm.
effects: Creates a tamper-evident record.
May embed or link the attestation to the asset.

functions.name: Verify attestation
functions.description: Validate signature, time-stamp, revocation, content binding and, where applicable, SLSA builder pairing.
preconditions: Trust list and time source are configured.
effects: Sets well-formed, valid or trusted state.
Does not judge whether content is good or authentic in a moral sense.

functions.name: Validate provenance constraints
functions.description: Normalize a PROV instance and check uniqueness, ordering, typing and impossibility constraints.
preconditions: Instance uses PROV types and relations or a documented mapping.
effects: Marks the instance valid or invalid.
Does not add missing history.

functions.name: Locate and query provenance
functions.description: Discover provenance-URIs or query services for a target and retrieve records, possibly from multiple providers.
preconditions: Either a Link header, HTML or RDF relation, or a known service-URI is available.
effects: Returns zero or more records.
Does not imply any record is authoritative.

functions.name: Redact assertion
functions.description: Remove or zero an assertion while declaring the redaction so remaining bindings can still be validated.
preconditions: Hard bindings that would break are excluded or rewritten per the C2PA redaction rules.
effects: Hides the assertion content.
Records that redaction occurred.

functions.name: Register pingback
functions.description: POST downstream provenance-URIs to a published pingback endpoint so the original publisher can discover later uses.
preconditions: Pingback URI was advertised for the target.
effects: May store or ignore the URIs according to publisher policy.
Does not grant the poster write access to the original record.

composition.target: Entity, Artifact, Dataset, Content or Physical Object subject models
composition.purpose: Attach a governed provenance graph and optional attestations to any subject whose origin, derivation, custody or production history must be recorded.
Cite responsibility-bearers without duplicating identity, contact or legal-person data.
Cite where an activity, entity, agent or event occurred without owning geometry or gazetteers.
Point at rights statements that constrained use or derivation; do not encode licence terms here.
Use PROV-DM types, relations and PROV-CONSTRAINTS validity as the default graph semantics; do not claim instance validity unless constraints are checked.
Align Object, Event, Agent and digital-provenance events for preservation repositories.
Align cryptographically bound manifests, actions, ingredients and trust validation for media assets.
Align software production provenance, builder trust boundaries and digest-identified subjects.
Align legal title versus physical custody and actor participation for cultural objects.
Align LI_Lineage statement, sources and process steps for geographic and other dataset resources.
Align what-when-where-why-how traceability events and chain of custody for supply-chain assets.
Align Provenance Information as one PDI component alongside Reference, Context, Fixity and Access Rights.
Align narrative ownership and custody statements and the PROV-DC mapping of agency, date and derivation terms, recording that the mapping is partial.
Allow quality assessments to consume lineage without storing quality results in this mixin.
Distinguish production history from contents of an artifact.

owner_package_requirements: Designate a Dimension owner accountable for minting record identifiers, choosing aligned profiles (PROV, PREMIS, C2PA, SLSA, CIDOC, ISO 19115, EPCIS) and declaring which constraints are enforced.
Publish a namespace IRI for local identifiers and a mapping from foreign master-system identifiers to that namespace.
Maintain trust-list, TSA, builder-id and claim-generator acceptance policy as versioned configuration, not as ad hoc per-record data.
Record both event time and ingestion time on every accepted record, using RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# for PROV terms; adopt C2PA, SLSA, PREMIS, CIDOC, ISO 19115 and GS1 namespaces only as alignment annotations. Local Dimension identifiers should live under a Dimension-owned IRI; UUID or ULID is a fallback when no master-system or governed IRI exists.

canonicalization_rules: Treat identifiers as case-sensitive except where the originating scheme says otherwise.
Interpret unset, null and empty attestation fields as equivalent when consuming SLSA or in-toto predicates.
Normalize PROV instances per PROV-CONSTRAINTS before comparing for equivalence; compare normal forms up to existential-variable isomorphism.
Hash-based subject identity is canonical for software and media bindings; URI identity is canonical for PROV entities that are not byte-stable.
Do not treat a date or timestamp as an identifier.
patch_rules: Provenance assertions already included in a signed claim MUST NOT be silently rewritten; add a new activity that generates a new entity or a new signed record.
Redaction is the only in-place concealment and MUST leave a declaration.
Patches to unsigned working graphs MAY merge attributes of the same identified object if unification succeeds; failed unification is invalid.
Extension fields MUST NOT alter the meaning of standard fields.
compatibility_rules: Consumers SHOULD accept both qualified and unqualified PROV forms and treat qualified as implying unqualified.
C2PA validators SHOULD ignore unknown constructs from newer spec versions rather than rejecting the whole manifest, while recording partial interpretation.
SLSA predicateType major version is the compatibility boundary; minor versions are monotonic.
Alignment with Dublin Core, PREMIS or ISO 19115 is partial; do not claim round-trip equivalence.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier from the minting repository, builder, camera, archive or custody register.
Governed global identifier or IRI, including PROV qualified names, C2PA URNs, SLSA builder.id URIs and EPCIS event IDs.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or governed identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record event time and observation or ingestion time separately; do not use a date as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifact names are the record kind plus master identifier, for example prov-bundle-{id}, c2pa-manifest-{urn}, slsa-provenance-{subjectDigest}, premis-event-{eventId}, epcis-event-{eventID}.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Signed or hashed artifacts MUST record algorithm, digest or signature, signer or builder, and optional time-stamp; verify before trust; treat detached records as incomplete until rebound via hard or soft binding.

policies: Do not infer that a valid, well-formed or signed provenance record means the subject is authentic, lawful, unbiased or good.
Honor creator control and privacy: omit or redact personal provenance fields when the creator withheld them, and do not reconstruct withheld identity from side channels.
When multiple providers supply contradictory records, keep all records, attribute each to its provider, and apply an explicit selection policy rather than overwriting.
Deletion of a subject does not imply deletion of its provenance when OAIS or legal-hold policy requires keeping history of destruction; record invalidation as an event.

read: Any caller with bundle-scope read may retrieve non-redacted assertions and validation reports.
Artifact-scope read is required for signatures, certificates and raw hashes.
Existence of a record MAY be concealed when existence is sensitive.
create: Create is allowed to authorized claim generators, builders, preservation events and custody registrars.
Create MUST mint or capture a master identifier and record generated_at and ingested_at.
Create of a signed attestation MUST occur inside the declared trust boundary for SLSA Build L2 or higher.
update: Signed records are immutable; updates append a new entity, activity or successor manifest.
Unsigned working graphs may merge attributes under uniqueness constraints.
Redaction is a controlled update that conceals content and declares the concealment.
delete: Delete of working unsigned drafts is allowed to owners.
Delete of signed or archived records requires retention review and SHOULD emit an invalidation or deaccession event.

roles.name: Claim generator
responsibilities: Bind to subject identifiers or digests.
Request signature by an authorized signer.

roles.name: Signer or builder control plane
responsibilities: Guarantee authenticity of attested fields within the trust boundary.

roles.name: Custodian or registrar
responsibilities: Maintain chain continuity including unknown-source and loss events.

roles.name: Validator or consumer
responsibilities: Present trust signals without value judgement.
Isolate the correct target-URI among multiple entities in a record.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Set identifier policy, alignment profile, retention and access defaults.

access.default_rule: Deny read of signed credentials, personal agent attributes and redacted assertions; allow read of non-sensitive graph summaries to authenticated Dimension users; existence MAY be denied when sensitive.
exceptions: Public C2PA or SLSA attestations intended for consumers MAY be world-readable.
Legal process and preservation audit MAY override default deny on archived records.
Pingback POST is write-limited to appending provenance-URIs, not editing the original record.
audit_requirements: Log create, verify, redact, custody-transfer, pingback and delete with actor, record_id, event_time and ingested_at.
Retain validation reports for as long as the attestation they describe.
Do not log withheld personal fields that were never stored.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Read the Specification URL for this Provenance mixin semantics before any storage-specific projection.
Read Storage type URL and Interface URL only as projections of the mixin, not as alternate semantics.
Read Processes URL for assert, verify, query, redact, custody-transfer and retention operations.

coverage.claim: This mixin covers the defensible union of W3C PROV graph semantics, preservation events, media content credentials, software build attestations, cultural-heritage custody versus title, dataset lineage, supply-chain traceability events and OAIS provenance information, as a format-neutral attachment to other subjects. It is not a universal theory of history, authenticity or trust.

checklist.notes: Record, subject, entity, activity, agent, builder, signer and event identifiers with master-system, IRI then UUID/ULID priority.
Generation, usage, start, end, invalidation, revision, deaccession and deletion-as-event.
Derivation, communication, attribution, association, delegation, membership, specialization, alternate, ingredients and custody transfers.
Event time versus observation or ingestion time; RFC 3339; PROV event ordering without assuming one global clock.
The mixin is provenance; provenance-of-provenance is covered via bundles, manifests and attribution of records.
Attribution of entities, CIDOC title versus custody, Dublin Core provenance statements and rightsHolder as a reference only.
PROV-CONSTRAINTS validity, C2PA well-formed/valid/trusted states, SLSA verification and fixity checks.
PROV-AQ discovery and query, OAIS access rights, default-deny on sensitive fields, existence-sensitivity.
Invalidation, archive retention, legal hold, ingest-first optional PDI, and deletion as a recorded event.
Alignments to PROV, PREMIS, C2PA, SLSA, in-toto, CIDOC, ISO 19115, EPCIS, OAIS and Dublin Core with explicit partial-mapping caveats.
Hard and soft bindings, signatures, time-stamps, revocation and builder trust boundaries.
C2PA redaction declarations and creator control over inclusion of provenance data.
Location of events and entities as references; geometries left to a Place sibling.

known_omissions: Forensic laboratory chain-of-custody procedures (for example ASTM E1492 or SWGDE) lack a primary source adopted in this pass and remain a sibling gap.
ISO 23494 biotechnology provenance and related lab-sample standards were not grounded in a retrieved primary text.
ML training-data lineage, model-card provenance and dataset-licence enforcement have no single primary standard equivalent to PROV or C2PA; C2PA AI disclosure is only an alignment.
Quantum-safe signature migration for long-term archives is unspecified by the cited primary sources.
1970 UNESCO cultural-property export rules and national patrimony statutes are legal overlays, not technical provenance types.
Live multi-hop reconstruction of implicit PROV blank nodes from sparse Dublin Core records is an implementation strategy, not a required Dimension behaviour.
Region-specific eIDAS or national trust-list programmes beyond the C2PA Trust List are not enumerated.
conflicts: ISO 19115-1:2014 defines provenance, citing ISO 5127, as the organization or individual that created, accumulated, maintained and used records, and defines lineage as provenance plus sources and production processes. W3C PROV uses provenance for the latter graph. Alignment must keep both senses labelled.
Dublin Core dct:provenance is a narrative custody and ownership statement; PROV is a graph. PROV-DC maps the property to prov:has_provenance, not to wasAttributedTo.
CIDOC separates legal title from physical custody; Dublin Core and many supply-chain practices lump them. Collapsing them is a Dimension choice, not conformance.
C2PA refuses value judgements of good or bad; SLSA Build levels are assurance grades of production integrity. Do not equate a trusted C2PA manifest with SLSA Build L3.
PROV unique-generation forbids two generations of one entity in a valid instance; Dublin Core created plus issued on one resource is common and is valid PROV only if modelled as specializations.
C2PA v2 removed identified humans from assertions for privacy; PREMIS and PROV still treat Person agents as first-class. Sharing profiles must not re-identify withheld actors.
ISO 14721:2025 allows information packages where PDI is optional (ingest first, describe later); OAIS users of earlier editions expected Provenance Information as part of PDI.
in-toto and SLSA treat the builder as a trust boundary that must not be tenant-controlled for authenticity; PROV allows any agent to assert provenance, with trust decided separately.
regional_assumptions: RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offsets are required even where local archives store civil dates only.
C2PA Trust List and X.509-only signing reflect a primarily industry PKI practice; other regions may require eIDAS or national PKI profiles as additional acceptance policy.
CIDOC title versus custody is expressed for museum practice and may not match common-law versus civil-law transfer of stolen goods; legal title outcome is out of scope.
EPCIS adoption in pharmaceutical traceability (for example DSCSA in the United States) is a jurisdictional overlay on the same event model, not a separate provenance type.
English is the normative language of the cited W3C Recommendations; translations are non-normative.
adversarial_checks: Would treating this mixin as an entity rather than a mixin duplicate Artifact, Event or Agent models? Mitigated by MIX-IN composition and explicit out-of-scope list.
Would claiming ISO 19115 or C2PA conformance without constraint or trust-list evidence be a false conformance claim? Mitigated by ALIGN not EXTEND and by recording conflicts.
Would a date-stamped filename be used as a provenance identifier? Forbidden by identity priority and timestamp rule.
Would a valid signature be presented as proof that media is true? Forbidden by C2PA non-goals and policy text.
Would withheld personal actor data be reconstructed from EXIF or logs? Forbidden by privacy policy and C2PA v2 removal of identified humans from assertions.
Would tenant-generated SLSA fields be treated as control-plane authentic? Explicit tenant-generated field question and builder trust boundary.
Would deletion of an object erase evidence of its destruction? Invalidation and retention policy require a recorded event when archive policy applies.
